_about: Snapshot of the annotation keywords of spec/grid-schema.schema.json and spec/ir.schema.json taken on 2026-11-03, before the plain-language rewrite of task #3561 (DS-20). descriptions and comments map the JSON Pointer of the schema node to the keyword's text, byte for byte; skeletonSha256 is the SHA-256 of the schema without any string-valued description or $comment key, as canonical JSON (sorted keys, no spaces, UTF-8). See scripts/test_schema_descriptions.py.

descriptions: The host-declared field allowlist and per-field configuration every compilation requires (SC-1..SC-5). This is a spec-level assumption authored for the conformance fixture suite (#1630) ahead of the actual GridSchema model/validator (#1631) — #1631 must conform to this shape, not the other way around, since this schema exists first. That precedence applies to what existed then; members added later were added here and in the model by the same story ('source' in #1638, per-field 'format' in #1653), so for those two the two are one change and neither leads. Every field a compilation touches (in filters, sort, group, aggregations) MUST appear in 'fields'; a colId absent from 'fields' is what the allowlist (SC-1) exists to reject.
descriptions./properties/mode: SC-1: Strict throws on an unlisted colId; Lenient silently strips it. Strict is the default per the TRD's own [DEFAULT] marker.
descriptions./properties/source: The physical collection every compiled query reads from: the SQL table or view named in FROM, the MongoDB collection, the Search index. Host-declared and never client-influenced — exactly like the per-field 'physical' mappings (SC-4) beside it, which is why it belongs here and not on the wire request: no AG Grid payload carries it and a compiler cannot invent it. Required — a query with no source cannot be emitted at all. Added in #1638: before it existed, every expected artifact in the fixture suite named a table ('FROM employees') that appeared in none of that fixture's inputs, recoverable only from the directory name.
descriptions./properties/stableKey: SEM-6: the field appended as a trailing sort tiebreaker whenever the request's own sort, after SEM-6's reduction (a field listed once, the sort stopping at an exact stable key), doesn't already reach a unique key. Required per grid — every GridSchema fixture must declare one, and it must itself be a key present in 'fields'.
descriptions./properties/staticFilter: SC-5: a host-authored IR filter fragment ANDed into every compiled query (the tenancy/soft-delete hook). Never client-influenced — this field only ever appears in schema.json, never in an agGridRequest.json. Absent means no static filter for this fixture.
descriptions./properties/fields: SC-2: the exhaustive allowlist, keyed by logical colId.
descriptions./$defs/fieldConfig/properties/type: The declared type used by the AG Grid adapter to coerce this field's wire values into a typedValue (SEM-5) — matches the type tags in ir.schema.json's $defs/typedValue one-for-one.
descriptions./$defs/fieldConfig/properties/aggregatab: Subset of AR-8's closed v1 aggregation functions this field may be aggregated with. Empty/absent means not aggregatable.
descriptions./$defs/fieldConfig/properties/physical: SC-4: per-backend physical mapping. A field need only declare mappings for the backends the fixture actually targets.
descriptions./$defs/fieldConfig/properties/text: SC-3: only meaningful when type is 'string'.
descriptions./$defs/fieldConfig/properties/exportable: EXP-1: whether this field is included by default in a CSV/TSV export when the request's exportColumns is absent (§6.1: 'all schema fields flagged exportable are emitted in schema order'). true by default.
descriptions./$defs/fieldConfig/properties/label: EXP-1: the export header text for this field when exportColumns doesn't supply its own header override ('headers from schema labels'). Falls back to the field's colId when absent.
descriptions./$defs/fieldConfig/properties/format: EXP-5: per-field format overrides for the CSV/TSV writer. Absent means the invariant-culture default. Host-declared and never client-influenced — no AG Grid request carries a format, which is why EXP-5 puts the override in schema config. Like 'label', it reaches no compiler and appears in no expected artifact: page-export/026 is 013's inputs with these overrides added and pins a byte-identical postgres.artifact.json. Added in #1653.
descriptions./$defs/physicalMapping/properties/sql: SC-4: plain column, qualified column (t.col), or a raw SQL expression escape hatch — always declared server-side, never client-influenced.
descriptions./$defs/physicalMapping/properties/search: SC-3: the .keyword-style exact-match/substring sub-field name, for term/wildcard/prefix/regexp ops on an analyzed field.

SC-3 (plural sub-field names): a keyword sub-field maintained via an ICU-folding normalizer at index time, used for case-insensitive ORDER BY / range comparisons (SEM-1) where ES/OpenSearch's query-time case_insensitive parameter is unavailable (range queries, in the pinned 7.10-era subset). Distinct from keywordSubField — only declare it for a field that needs case-insensitive ordering.
descriptions./$defs/formatOptions: EXP-5's two per-field overrides, and only those two: the requirement names a date pattern and a decimal separator, so a third (thousands separator, boolean spelling, culture name) would be an invention every language port then has to reproduce.
descriptions./$defs/formatOptions/properties/datePatt: EXP-5's date pattern, replacing the writer's ISO 8601 default for this field only. Only meaningful when type is 'date' or 'datetime'. Written in the LDML/CLDR field letters every platform's formatter shares — yyyy, MM, dd, HH, mm, ss and literal separators — so 'dd/MM/yyyy' means the same to .NET, Java and a JavaScript port; a pattern outside that shared subset is not portable and must not appear in a fixture. A pattern no formatter can apply is rejected when the schema is parsed, not when the first date cell is written, which a streaming export cannot recover from. Note that an offset specifier (z/K) renders the host machine's offset when applied to a value that carries none, so it is meaningful only for a column an adapter yields with an offset.
descriptions./$defs/formatOptions/properties/decimalS: EXP-5's decimal separator for this field, overriding the writer-wide default ('.', invariant culture). Only meaningful when type is 'decimal' or 'double' — an integral value has no fractional part to separate. Equal to the writer's active delimiter this is EXP-5's collision, and it is the same defect as the writer-wide one: the export is refused before its first byte by the writer, the only party that knows the delimiter. See schemas/writer-config.schema.json for the writer-wide default this overrides.
descriptions./$defs/textOptions/properties/caseSensit: SEM-1: per-field opt-in to case-sensitive comparison; insensitive is the IR-level default.
descriptions./$defs/textOptions/properties/searchMode: SEM-7: substring is contains' pinned default (wildcard/ngram); analyzed is the explicit per-field opt-in to tokenized relevance matching.

descriptions: Canonical, vendor-neutral intermediate representation (IR) for a grid query: filter tree + sort + group + aggregation + page spec (see docs/TRD-grid-query-compiler.md AR-2 layer 2, AR-5..AR-9). This is the language-neutral source of truth (AR-1) — language implementations conform to this document, never the reverse. It is a structural contract only: resource limits (max depth, max leaves, max in-values, max page size — SEC-3) are entirely runtime-validator concerns, deliberately not encoded here as structural bounds, because SEC-3 requires them configurable per host and a schema-level maxItems cannot vary per instance. The runtime validator MUST run its limit checks (including the max-depth check against filterNode's unbounded recursion) before or during descent into the document — never only after full structural parse — so a depth/leaf bomb is rejected cleanly (SEC-6) rather than exhausting the stack first. The $id path is versioned (/v1/) per P-2: a future breaking IR revision publishes at /v2/ alongside this one, never overwriting it.
descriptions./properties/filter: Root of the filter tree (AR-5). Absent means no filtering is applied.
descriptions./properties/sort: Ordered sort spec (AR-9): applied in array order, first element is the primary sort key. Absent is the only encoding of 'no sort' — an empty array is rejected (minItems: 1) so the document has one canonical form per PERF-2's cache-key hashing and ML-3's byte-comparable fixtures.
descriptions./properties/group: Row-group spec for the AG Grid SSRM drill-down protocol (AR-8). Absent means the request is not grouped.
descriptions./properties/aggregations: Aggregation spec (AR-8): (field, func) pairs computed for grouped rows. Absent is the only encoding of 'no aggregations' — an empty array is rejected (minItems: 1), for the same canonical-form reason as 'sort'.
descriptions./properties/page: Page spec (AG-3, EXP-2): a bounded row range, or 'none' for unpaginated export/streaming output.
descriptions./$defs/filterNode: A node of the filter tree (AR-5). Recursive by construction so a runtime validator can walk it to count depth/leaves against the configurable SEC-3 limits (default max depth 8, max leaves 64) — this schema deliberately carries no maxItems/maxDepth structural bound here, because SEC-3 limits are configurable per host and a fixed schema bound cannot vary per instance (see the root description for the required check-ordering).
descriptions./$defs/andNode: Logical conjunction of child nodes (AR-5: And(nodes[])).
descriptions./$defs/andNode/properties/nodes: Child filter nodes, all of which must match. No maxItems here: SEC-3's max-leaves limit is a tree-wide budget enforced by the runtime validator, not a per-node arity bound — a fixed maxItems on this array would neither express nor enforce that budget correctly.
descriptions./$defs/orNode: Logical disjunction of child nodes (AR-5: Or(nodes[])).
descriptions./$defs/orNode/properties/nodes: Child filter nodes, at least one of which must match. See andNode.nodes for why there is no maxItems here.
descriptions./$defs/notNode: Logical negation of a single child node (AR-5: Not(node)).
descriptions./$defs/comparisonNode: A leaf comparison against a single field (AR-5: Comparison(field, op, value|values)). Split into per-operator-category subschemas because the value shape differs: no value (unary), one typed value (binary), a typed-value array (set), or a typed from/to pair with inclusivity flags (range).
descriptions./$defs/unaryComparisonNode: Comparison operators that take no value: null/blank checks (SEM-2) and the boolean-filter shorthand ops (AR-6).
descriptions./$defs/binaryComparisonNode: Comparison operators that take exactly one typed value (AR-6).
descriptions./$defs/setComparisonNode: Set-membership operators (AR-6: in, notIn) — a typed-value array that MAY be empty (SEM-8: `in []` matches no row, `notIn []` matches every row). No maxItems here: SEC-3's max-in-values limit is host-configurable, so a fixed schema bound would reject a legitimately higher-configured host's IR; the runtime validator is the sole enforcement point.
descriptions./$defs/rangeComparisonNode: The inRange operator (AR-6) with explicit per-boundary inclusivity flags — never left implicit, since defaults differ by filter type (SEM-4).
descriptions./$defs/fieldName: The logical field name (colId) as declared in the host's GridSchema allowlist (SC-1, SC-2). Never a physical column/path — that mapping is resolved by the compiler from schema config, not carried in the IR. maxLength is a structural amplification cap, not the allowlist check itself (SC-1/SEC-1 membership is a runtime concern this schema cannot express).
descriptions./$defs/unaryOperator: AR-6 closed operator set, no-value subset.
descriptions./$defs/binaryOperator: AR-6 closed operator set, single-value subset.
descriptions./$defs/setOperator: AR-6 closed operator set, value-array subset.
descriptions./$defs/operator: The full AR-6 closed operator set (17 operators, no others) — the union of every category. Provided for consumers that want a single flat enum rather than the per-category subschemas used by comparisonNode.
descriptions./$defs/typedValue: A fully-typed IR value (AR-7). Every value is tagged with its declared type; compilers never infer or guess a type from JSON's native number/string distinction. Frontend adapters resolve AG Grid's stringly-typed wire values into one of these using the field's declared type before the IR is built.
descriptions./$defs/stringValue/properties/value: Structural amplification cap (not a SEC-3 named limit — SEC-3 covers tree shape/page size, not string length). Generous headroom over typical grid-cell text; a host needing longer values should not be routing them through a filter comparison.
descriptions./$defs/int64Value: 64-bit integer (AR-7 distinguishes int64 from decimal/double, never a generic 'number'). Bounded to the signed 64-bit range so every port can round-trip it in a native int64/long; note the TypeScript port (ML-1 step 2) must special-case values beyond +/-2^53 since JSON.parse loses precision there — deserialize int64 as a bigint or string in that port, not a JS number.
descriptions./$defs/decimalValue: Arbitrary-precision decimal (AR-7). Carried as a numeric string rather than a JSON number to avoid float round-tripping loss.
descriptions./$defs/dateValue: Local date, no time-of-day or zone component (AR-7). 'format: date' is annotation-only per the draft 2020-12 default meta-schema (not every port's validator asserts it — Ajv needs ajv-formats, Python jsonschema needs a format_checker, etc.), so 'pattern' carries the actual cross-language guarantee (G4); format is kept alongside it as a hint for tooling that does assert it.
descriptions./$defs/datetimeValue: An instant plus its interpretation zone (AR-7, SEM-4 — dates & zones). 'value' is an ISO-8601 timestamp with an explicit offset/Z; 'zone' (an IANA time zone id) records the zone used to resolve the instant, needed for the zone rules in TRD §7.4. See dateValue for why 'pattern' accompanies 'format' here too.
descriptions./$defs/datetimeValue/properties/zone: An IANA time zone id (e.g. 'Europe/Paris', 'UTC') — not allowlisted anywhere (unlike 'field'), so this shape constraint is the only structural guard against a malformed value reaching a dialect-specific zone clause (AT TIME ZONE / $dateTrunc.timezone / ES time_zone).
descriptions./$defs/nullValue: The null value (AR-7). Distinct from the blank/notBlank operators, which are a separate SEM-2 null-handling concern at the comparison-node level rather than a value.
descriptions./$defs/groupSpec: AG Grid SSRM row-group drill-down protocol (AR-8). groupKeys.length < groupCols.length compiles a grouped query (next group column + aggregations, filtered by the consumed keys); equal length compiles the leaf query (BM-2).
descriptions./$defs/groupSpec/properties/groupCols: Ordered list of row-group column field names, as configured on the grid. maxItems is a structural amplification cap, not a SEC-3 named limit (those stay host-configurable and out of this schema, per the root description): groupSpec is as client-controlled as the filter tree, GRP-5 compiles each consumed key into one leaf predicate, and a host may hand a groupSpec straight to a compiler without passing the SEC-3 validator at all — so N needs a bound that holds on every path. 64 is SEC-3's own DEFAULT max-leaves, which makes a structurally valid groupSpec unable to exceed that budget by itself; a host configuring a smaller maxLeaves still gets the tighter answer from the runtime validator.
descriptions./$defs/groupSpec/properties/groupKeys: Group key values already consumed by the drill-down so far, one per already-expanded group level, in groupCols order. Each key is a typedValue (AR-7) — a group key is compiled into an equality predicate against its group column (BM-2), i.e. it is a filter value like any other, so it must be typed the same way; an untyped JSON scalar here would force every compiler to re-guess the type AR-7 exists to make explicit. A drilled-into null group bucket is nullValue, not JSON null. maxItems repeats groupCols' cap for the same amplification reason: GRP-1's groupKeys.length <= groupCols.length is a cross-array comparison JSON Schema cannot express, so structural validation alone would otherwise leave this array unbounded.
descriptions./$defs/setValuesSpec: BM-3's set-filter distinct-values request (GRP-6 in spec/semantics.md). Deliberately a $def rather than a property of the root document: the root models a row-fetch query and REQUIRES 'page', while a distinct-values query has no page at all (its limit is a ceiling, not a window), no sort and no aggregation — and restructuring the root into a two-armed oneOf would be a breaking change to a published /v1/ contract. The wire envelope this mirrors ('setValuesRequest') is Craticula's own synthetic shape, not AG Grid's: AG Grid Community has no request/response type for set-filter values at all and delegates the whole job to a host-supplied SetFilterParams.values callback. See spec/fixtures/group-aggregation/README.md for the envelope and 016-019 for its artifact oracle.
descriptions./$defs/setValuesSpec/properties/colId: The column whose distinct values are being resolved: the SELECT DISTINCT expression, the sole ORDER BY key, and the field whose OWN conditions are dropped from the accompanying filter (GRP-6). Client-controlled, and unlike a filter's colId it is the question rather than a condition on it — so it must pass the SC-1 allowlist in EVERY GridSchema mode, Lenient included.
descriptions./$defs/setValuesSpec/properties/searchPr: The set filter's own inline search box text. Compiled into an ordinary startsWith predicate against colId (GRP-6), so SEM-1's per-field mechanism and SEM-7's escaping govern it exactly as they would a user's own prefix filter — it is not a construct of its own, and it survives the own-field exclusion that removes every other condition on colId. An empty search box OMITS this property; minLength:1 rejects "", which would otherwise compile to a predicate matching every row. maxLength repeats stringValue's own bound, since it compiles into exactly one.
descriptions./$defs/setValuesSpec/properties/limit: A client-requested cap on how many distinct values come back. Never authoritative: the host's configured maximum always wins and an absent value falls back to the host's configured default, i.e. the compiled cap is min(limit ?? default, maximum) — GRP-6. Exceeding the maximum is NOT a rejection (the server clamps and answers), which is why no maxItems-style bound appears here; those two numbers are SEC-3 limits and, per the root description, stay host-configurable and out of this schema. minimum:1 is structural rather than a SEC-3 limit: a non-positive cap is not 'no cap', it is a request that can never return a value.
descriptions./$defs/aggregation: A single (field, func) aggregation pair (AR-8). func is limited to {sum, min, max, avg, count} in v1 — first/last are explicitly excluded (v2 roadmap).
descriptions./$defs/aggregation/properties/alias: Optional output key for the aggregated value; defaults to a compiler-chosen name derived from field+func when absent. Unlike 'field', alias is not gated by the GridSchema allowlist, yet it lands in generated query text as an identifier (SUM(x) AS <alias>, $group output key, ES agg name) where SEC-2's 'values are parameters' rule cannot apply — an identifier can't be parameterized. The identifier-safe pattern is therefore the only guard against alias-as-injection-vector across all four compilers.
descriptions./$defs/aggregationFunc: AR-8 closed v1 aggregation function set. 'first'/'last' are v2 roadmap, deliberately excluded here.
descriptions./$defs/sortItem: A single sort key (AR-9). nullsPosition is always explicit in the IR — never left to a backend's default ordering (SEM-3).
descriptions./$defs/nullsPosition: Explicit null-ordering (AR-9, SEM-3) — never inferred from direction.
descriptions./$defs/pageSpec: AG-3 startRow/endRow paging, or the unpaginated 'none' mode required for full-export compilation (EXP-2).
descriptions./$defs/rangePage: A bounded row range, mirroring AG Grid SSRM's startRow/endRow (AG-3). endRow is exclusive, matching the SSRM convention.
descriptions./$defs/rangePage/properties/endRow: Zero-based exclusive end offset. (endRow - startRow) is the requested page size. This schema cannot express either the SEC-3 max-page-size cap (host-configurable, so no fixed 'maximum' belongs here) or the endRow >= startRow invariant (cross-property comparison is inexpressible in draft 2020-12) — both are runtime-validator obligations; do not assume either is enforced by structural validation alone.
descriptions./$defs/nonePage: Unpaginated mode (EXP-2): compile the full filtered+sorted artifact with no row-range clause, for streaming/export scopes such as EXP-1's exportScope: 'all'.

comments./$defs/setValuesSpec/properties/searchPr: A prefix against a column not declared 'string' has no defined meaning and is rejected at the typeCoercion stage (SEM-5's uncoercible-value), which JSON Schema cannot express: it depends on the GridSchema, not on this document.
